text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam exported 500,000 tonnes of rice in May, bringing the total since the beginning of this year to 1.33 million tonnes, a 50-percent jump from the same period of last year.
-- Vietnam is to hold regular investment forums to encourage foreign investment.
-- The flow of electricity on the 500 KV North-South tranmission line has been reversed to supply the north with 300-400 MW per day during the current shortage.
-- The First Vice President of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Hassan Habibi, will pay an official visit to vietnam from June 18-21.
-- Turkmenistan beat Vietnam 4-0 in their World Cup Asian zone group eight qualifying match in Ho Chi Minh City on Sunday.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has decided to conduct an annual survey on labour and employement between now and 2000 as part of efforts to reduce the unemployment rate.
-- Vietnamese enterprises' export earnings from agricultural products were $52.1 million in May, a rise of 17.5 percent from the same month in 1996.
-- The use of electricity for trapping and killing rats has been forbidden by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development.

-- Two hundred and eight employees of the Vietnam Industrial and Commercial Bank who violated banking regulations have been disciplined. The Bank has recovered 340.87 billion dong ($29.2 million) of its overdue debts.
